sections.title: Which digit tells us how to round?
sections.label: Round
sections.intro: The requested precision tells you which digit to keep. The next digit decides whether it changes.

blocks.html: If the next digit is 0 to 4, keep the last digit. If it is 5 to 9, increase the last digit and carry if needed.

sections.title: What is the biggest group count that works?
sections.label: Factors
sections.intro: Two totals can be split into the same number of equal groups only when that group count divides both totals exactly.

blocks.html: List or pair factors of each number. The highest common factor is the greatest value on both lists.

figure.alt: Factor, ×, Factor, Product
figure.caption: A factor is part of a product. The product is a multiple of both factors.

blocks.prompt:
A club has 35 pencils and 21 stickers. It uses all the items to make identical packs.

Find the greatest possible number of packs.
blocks.hint: Find the highest common factor.
blocks.solution:
The number of packs must divide both 35 and 21 exactly.

The greatest shared divisor is 7.

\(7\).

sections.title: How do we add mixed numbers?
sections.label: Mixed
sections.intro: A mixed number shows some whole objects and part of another. When two small parts are added, they may make an extra whole.

blocks.html:
Add the whole-number parts directly. Give the fractional parts a shared denominator, so the pieces are the same size.

  1. Add the whole-number parts.
  2. Use equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then add the numerators.
  3. If the fraction reaches one whole, regroup and simplify.

Carry a whole across if the fraction sum is at least 1.

blocks.html:
Give both fractions the same denominator to count same-sized pieces when that is easy. A general method is to keep the first fraction and multiply by the reciprocal of the non-zero divisor.

Use a common factor to simplify the result.

sections.title: When is it easier to cancel first?

blocks.html:
Either add inside the bracket first, or distribute the outside factor. Distribution is often quicker when a denominator shares a factor with the number outside.

  1. Check whether the fractions inside the bracket have a common denominator already.
  2. If you distribute, multiply both inside terms by the factor.
  3. Check your result by trying the other method.

Calculate \(\frac{3}{4}\div\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{4}\times2=\frac32\). The answer is one and a half lengths.

revision.body:
How can we share a total equally?

The mean is the sum divided by the number of observations. The result need not be one of the original values.

Which number is in the middle?

The median can be more useful than the mean if a very high or low value would pull the mean away from most of the data.

Do we need the most common value or the spread?

The range is largest minus smallest. A low range shows the whole set is contained within a small interval.

How can a frequency table help us summarise many values?

For each row, multiply value by frequency. Add these totals and divide by the sum of the frequencies.
